authority.assignable_by: the tool vendor or the official documentation of the provider
authority.label: vendor_documented
authority.meaning: An official provider or tool convention.
authority.promotion_rule: Never promoted by HQ; a local file cannot claim it.

authority.assignable_by: the HQ indexer during the census
authority.label: project_observed
authority.meaning: An actual repository file, observed in the census.
authority.promotion_rule: Observation never becomes current by itself.

authority.label: local_custom
authority.meaning: A local convention that has not been verified.
authority.promotion_rule: Must not be promoted without owner confirmation.

authority.label: proposed
authority.meaning: A candidate that has not been adopted.
authority.promotion_rule: Stays proposed until the owner accepts it.

authority.assignable_by: the indexer, when a path segment marks archive, history or donor material
authority.label: historical
authority.meaning: Archived or donor material. It stays historical.
authority.promotion_rule: Never promoted to current without an owner decision.

authority.label: owner
authority.promotion_rule: The only value that produces an accepted decision or a current CANON term.

authority.label: architecture
authority.meaning: Authority recorded by the architecture group.
authority.promotion_rule: Never promotes to `owner`; it is the default for extracted decisions and terms.

authority.label: agent_proposed
authority.meaning: A proposal raised by an agent.

authority.assignable_by: the extractor, when it reads an @hq:why or @hq:invariant annotation
authority.label: source_annotation
authority.meaning: A value observed in the source text rather than decided.
authority.promotion_rule: Never promotes to `owner`; it stays observed.

authority_notice: A document never grants execution authority. This taxonomy names what exists; it does not permit anything.

effects.description: Read a file from the local disk.
effects.rule: Allowed by default under the read scope; secret paths stay excluded by the walker.

effects.description: Create or change a file on the local disk.
effects.rule: Denied by default. Requires one of the write scopes or an explicit owner approval.

effects.description: Read rows from the local index.
effects.rule: Allowed by default under the read scope.

effects.description: Write rows to the local index.
effects.rule: Denied by default. Requires the index scope or an explicit owner approval.
Allowed by default under the read scope. A project without git falls back to a directory walk.

effects.description: Create a commit, a branch or a hook in a repository.
effects.rule: Denied by default. HQ installs its own managed hooks and never creates a commit, a branch or a push on its own.

effects.description: Send or receive data over the network.
effects.rule: HQ never performs a network effect. A component that declares one is refused at registration.

effects.description: Drive a browser or change provider state.
effects.rule: HQ never performs a browser effect. A component that declares one is refused at registration.

effects.description: Wait for an owner decision before continuing.
effects.rule: An approval gate is the only way a write effect may proceed without a standing scope, and the decision is recorded as a receipt.

effects.description: Send a message to a provider or a person.
effects.rule: HQ never sends. A component that declares a send effect is refused at registration.

entities.note: A registered directory with an absolute path; rows are created by `hq project add`.
entities.title: Project

entities.note: Every indexed Markdown, YAML or ADR file, classified into one of the 21 families plus `unclassified`.
entities.title: Document

entities.note: A dated outcome with rationale, alternatives, consequences and evidence.
entities.title: Decision

entities.note: A bounded term with a definition, aliases and explicit non-equivalences.
entities.title: CANON term

entities.note: One harness session recorded from the provider transcript.
entities.title: Session

entities.note: A single exchange inside a session. There is no `turn` table; docs/VIVIM-KB-INTAKE.md §8.4 lists `turn` under entitiesMissingTable, and turn text lives in `session_messages`.
entities.title: Turn

entities.note: A tiered memory row (`now`, `later`, `canon`) with origin, confidence and evidence.
entities.title: Note

entities.note: A declaration extracted from a source file by hq/lib/extract.mjs; rebuildable and never authoritative.
entities.title: Symbol

entities.note: One indexed file with its language, size, hash and mtime.
entities.title: File

entities.note: A git commit ingested into the event lake; immutable history, never rewritten.
entities.title: Commit

entities.note: The `events` table is declared in hq/lib/schema.mjs but no module in hq/lib inserts into it; the hq.event/1 store is contract-only (docs/AGENTIC-AUTOMATION-TOOLKIT.md §3).
entities.title: Event

entities.note: A versioned, declared action with effects and authority; the table is created by hq/lib/components.mjs, not by hq/lib/schema.mjs.
entities.title: Component

entities.note: A versioned DAG of component references with edges, defaults and config.
entities.title: Pipeline

entities.note: One execution of a pipeline version; the row records config, input and output digests.
entities.title: Run

entities.note: One attempt of one component inside a run.
entities.title: Step

entities.note: A scheduled unit of work with a lease and attempts; the table and its statuses are contract-only (docs/AGENTIC-AUTOMATION-TOOLKIT.md §5).
entities.title: Task

entities.note: The bounded, scored set of sources returned by hq/lib/context.mjs. It is not stored; the receipt that records it is.
entities.title: Context bundle

entities.note: An append-only evidence row: what was read, with source hashes and a digest.
entities.title: Receipt

entities.note: The KB domain model block (`hq.vivim-model/1`). No module stores it yet; hq/lib/kb-model.mjs is the planned projection.
entities.title: Model

entities.note: A KB-declared feature that names the flows and actions that deliver it.
entities.title: Feature

entities.note: A KB-declared given/when/then with a feature, a flow and evidence; the traceability spine.
entities.title: Use case

entities.note: A KB-declared action that materialises as an HQ component with its declared effects and authority copied verbatim.
entities.title: Action

entities.note: A KB-declared sequence of steps; HQ compiles it to a DAG view and rejects cycles.
entities.title: Flow

entities.note: A KB-declared origin of data (file, table, api, capture) with a trust level and an owner.
entities.title: Source

extension.definition: A request to add a term, an entity, a status, an effect, a scope or a schema id to the taxonomy.
extension.rule: The proposal names the new item, the reason it is needed and the surfaces that would use it.
extension.title: Proposal

extension.definition: The code, contract or observation that shows the new item is real.
extension.rule: No proposal advances without evidence that points at a file, a contract or a recorded observation.
extension.title: Evidence

extension.rule: Only the owner confirms. A document, an agent or a registry never confirms itself.
extension.title: Owner confirmation

extension.definition: A published revision of the taxonomy with a new version and a new digest.
extension.rule: A confirmed change publishes a new version. The previous version stays readable so old bundles still verify.
extension.title: New taxonomy version

extension.definition: A change that alters the meaning of an existing entry.
extension.rule: Never applied in place. The entry is amended by publishing a new version that records the change.
extension.title: No silent edit

extension.definition: Reusing an existing id for a different concept.
extension.rule: Never allowed. A different concept gets a new id; the old id keeps its meaning and its history.
extension.title: No redefinition

nonEquivalences.meaning: What a system knows about itself does not authorise it.
Being grounded in a source does not authorise an effect.
A confidence score is not a proof.
Reading a record is not performing an effect.
A stated intention is not completed work.
A displayed form is not the canonical identity of the record.
A rendered page carries no execution authority.
The name a record used to carry is not what it means now.
A document never becomes law by writing itself down.
A remembered fact is not permission.
Being able to act is not being allowed to act.
What was observed is not what was concluded.
The indexed copy of a record is not the record itself.
A context bundle is evidence of what was read, never permission to act.
A generated page documents a command; it never replaces it.
The console is a read-only lens over the same commands.
A declared model is not the code that implements it.
A use case that cites no evidence is not accepted.

scopes.rule: Every agent holds the read scope by default. It opens no write path.
Allows writing to the local index. It does not allow writing files outside the index.
Allows regenerating the derived wiki pages. A generated page is never authoritative.
Allows installing HQ-managed git hooks and the file watcher.
The owner scope is what makes a confirmation legal. It is granted by the owner, never by a document.
Covers the registry of spaces and the configuration. It does not imply a send or a browser effect.

statuses.rule: Only an explicit owner confirmation moves a decision to `accepted`. A document that claims `Accepted` is extracted as `proposed` and the claim is kept as evidence.
Only an explicit owner confirmation moves a term to `current`. A document that claims `current` is extracted as `provisional`.
A document has no manual status. The value is derived from the file path on every index run by the 217/133 registry, and `unclassified` is a real outcome rather than a failure.
An uncertain effect is reconciled read-only before any retry. A blind resend of an uncertain effect is forbidden.

statuses.drift: docs/COMPONENT-REGISTRY.md §5 mentions only `deprecated` and `retired` as moves; the module also allows `draft`, which is the default for a forked pipeline version.
statuses.rule: A published version is immutable. Retirement keeps the row queryable.
A published pipeline version is immutable; a change produces a new version with a parent link.

statuses.drift: No module emits the literal strings. The intake returns `ok: true` or `ok: false` plus `reasons[]` and `missingFromPackage[]`; `accepted` is `ok: true` with nothing missing, `refused` is `ok: false`, `partial` is `ok: true` with files reported missing from the package.
statuses.rule: A refusal is a receipt, not an exception: a refused package writes nothing.

statuses.drift: The stage list is declared in the contract; no module in hq/lib exports it yet.
statuses.rule: Stages are idempotent and cannot be skipped. `ready` requires owner confirmation and evidence.
A feature is declared by the KB. HQ reports which features have flows, actions and evidence; it never promotes one.

trust.meaning: The source is an official provider or tool convention.
trust.rule: Scores highest in a context bundle and may surface without a task-token match.

trust.meaning: The source is a file that was actually observed in the repository.
trust.rule: Scores below vendor material and above an unverified local convention.

trust.meaning: The source is a local convention that has not been verified.
trust.rule: Scores below observed material; a strong local convention still needs a task match to surface.

trust.drift: No numeric DCB weight is declared for `capture` in docs/DCB-PROTOCOL.md §3.2; only the five authority labels carry weights.
trust.meaning: The source is a runtime capture of what a provider actually returned.
trust.rule: Evidence of what was seen, never a declared standard. The KB model carries capture sources with a trust level; HQ keeps them out of the authority vocabulary.

trust.drift: No numeric DCB weight is declared for `inferred` in docs/DCB-PROTOCOL.md §3.2.
trust.meaning: The value was derived by HQ rather than read from a source.
trust.rule: Never an authority and never a substitute for evidence. It is recorded as inference, not as fact.

trust.drift: hq/lib/context.mjs docAuthority() does not read the registry authority label. It returns 1 for README.md and AGENTS.md, 0.6 for any other Markdown file and for anything under docs/, and 0 for everything else. The path heuristic is what the code does; the registry weights above are the declared model.
trust.rule: A context bundle scores each candidate with `1 + 3.6 * coverage + 1.2 * symbolBonus + 0.8 * recency + 0.6 * authority + 0.5 * proximity` and then selects under the token budget with an exact knapsack. The authority term is the only place trust enters the score.
trust.title: DCB scoring effect
